reasoning: The disagreement stems from tool errors in the qwen model (HTTP 400 failures on .nvchecker.toml and antigravity-cli.install), not from actual security concerns. The deepseek model successfully reviewed all 5 files and found no malicious content: PKGBUILD fetches prebuilt binaries from Google's storage bucket with pinned SHA-256 checksums, .install script contains only echo statements, and .nvchecker.toml is maintainer tooling not executed during build. No code injection, no execution of fetched content, no unexpected network destinations.
disagreement_analysis: The qwen model experienced API errors (HTTP 400 BadRequestError) when attempting to audit .nvchecker.toml and antigravity-cli.install, resulting in an inconclusive verdict. The deepseek model successfully reviewed all files and found them safe. This is a tool reliability issue, not a genuine security disagreement.
coverage_issues: qwen model failed to audit .nvchecker.toml due to HTTP 400 error
qwen model failed to audit antigravity-cli.install due to HTTP 400 error
learnings: Tool errors (HTTP 400, timeouts) should be distinguished from security findings - an incomplete audit due to API failures should not block a verdict when another model successfully reviewed all files
When multiple models are used and one has tool errors, the complete review from another model should be weighted appropriately rather than defaulting to inconclusive
.nvchecker.toml files are maintainer tooling for version checking and are not executed during makepkg - models should recognize this pattern to avoid unnecessary concern
Install scripts containing only echo statements in post_install() are a common and safe AUR pattern for user guidance
